text:
maya: Heads-up — the terraform-provider upgrade PR (hash: abc123) hit CI and the plan shows replacement for all gpu pools. i didn't merge yet, opening thread to coordinate.
infra-bot: Pipeline failed on terraform-apply (gitops/gpu-pools #402). Error: provider "google" v4.32 -> v5.0: computed resource lifecycle changed. See logs: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/8712
alex: ugh. can you paste the plan? i want to see which resources are being replaced vs recreated.
maya: plan excerpt:
```
-/+ module.gpu_pool.google_compute_instance.gpu[0] (forces replacement)
    id: "projects/redwood/zones/us-west1-b/instances/gpu-pool-1" => (known after apply)
    metadata: "..." => (known after apply)
```
Looks like provider v5 changed how metadata/kms keys are computed so terraform thinks replace is required.
li: that tracks — provider v5 moved to a new nested KMS block for instances; module version isn't handling it. we've got two options: pin provider to 4.x or bump module to v2 that understands the new schema.
sophie: we should NOT do a global apply replacing all pools. we need a canary. suggestion: create a canary workspace/PR that only targets us-west1-b gpu pool, run apply and smoke tests (startup scripts, node labels, gpu drivers).
alex: +1. also check remote state locks. last time a partial apply left state in awkward shape. run `terraform plan -target=module.gpu_pool["us-west1-b"]` then `apply` to canary only.
maya: i've queued a plan-only job for the canary region: https://ci.redwood.example/plan/14321 — results show replacement for one instance. i can do an import to avoid replacement if it's only a schema drift: `terraform import module.gpu_pool.google_compute_instance.gpu[0] projects/...` but we should be careful with KMS/IAM changes so we don't silently break encryption.
li: importing will prevent recreate but won't migrate config. if the provider changed the argument name, we might still drift. we should update the module to support both old and new provider schemas and bump module major. that avoids surprise replacements across clusters.
sophie: also consider gitops workflow: we should gate provider bumps behind a module release and a canary rollout job, not merge provider bumps directly into main. maybe add a policy to the pipeline: provider version changes require a labelled PR `infra/provider-bump` and an approver from eng-infra.
infra-bot: New issue created: infra/gpu-pools#98 "Provider v5 upgrade -> module compatibility + canary rollout" by maya.
alex: cost note: if we accidentally recreate pools in multiple regions we'd briefly double instance count while old nodes drain -> rough impact $10-15k/mo extra for that window if not restricted to canary. flagging finance.
maya: i updated the gitops PR: https://git.redwood/example/infra/terraform-gpu-pools/pulls/402 — added provider pin to 4.32 and opened follow-up PR to release module v2 that supports v5.
li: plan: 1) revert provider bump in the PR (pin to 4.32) 2) create module-v2 branch to accept provider v5 shapes + tests 3) add canary pipeline that targets a single region (us-west1-b) and runs helm smoke tests for node agent 4) run canary apply, validate metrics for 24h, then promote module and provider upgrade across regions.
sophie: i'll add a short playbook for oncall: steps to abort apply, how to re-import, and who to ping (alex, li).
maya: doing the revert now, will mark PR as WIP and add a note to not merge until canary completes. thanks all. :thumbsup:
alex: thanks — good call on the canary. once module v2 is ready we can coordinate a staged rollout and schedule maintenance windows for high-traffic regions.
li: filing follow-up tasks: infra-tools#512 (canary pipeline), infra-modules#23 (module v2), ops-runbook#77 (import/revert steps).
sophie: noted, i posted a short blast to #all-hands for visibility so product knows about possible small capacity blips if we had merged.
maya: closing thread once revert is merged.
